title: The Future of AI in Offensive Security
summary: Exploring how LLMs and autonomous agents are reshaping the landscape of penetration testing and vulnerability discovery.

steps.title: Reconnaissance with Autonomous Agents
steps.description: The first phase involves deploying a specialized LLM agent to map the target infrastructure. Unlike traditional scanners, these agents can understand context and identify non-obvious entry points.

steps.title: Vulnerability Synthesis
steps.description: Once the reconnaissance data is ingested, the AI synthesizes potential attack vectors by cross-referencing CVE databases with the specific configuration identified.

steps.title: Payload Generation & Execution
steps.description: The final step is the generation of a context-aware payload designed to exploit the synthesized vulnerability while remaining undetected by static analysis tools.

title: Securing Cloud Infrastructures at Scale
summary: Tactical guidelines for maintaining a fortress-level security posture in complex multi-cloud environments.

steps.title: Identity and Access Management Audit
steps.description: Initial audit of IAM roles and permissions to identify over-privileged accounts and potential privilege escalation paths.

steps.title: Network Perimeter Hardening
steps.description: Implementing strict security groups and NACLs to enforce the principle of least privilege at the network layer.

steps.title: Automated Compliance Monitoring
steps.description: Deploying automated scripts to continuously monitor the infrastructure for compliance with industry standards like CIS and SOC2.

title: PortSwigger: Information Disclosure in Error Messages
summary: Trigger a verbose error by sending text where the app expects a product ID, then read the framework version it leaks.

steps.title: Steps to solve
steps.description:
1. Open any product.
2. In the URL, change the product ID from a number to text, then read the error message.
3. Copy the framework version number shown in the error.
4. Go back to / and submit it as the solution.

title: PortSwigger: Information Disclosure on Debug Page
summary: Find a leftover phpinfo debug page with Burp Suite's content discovery and read the SECRET_KEY environment variable.

steps.title: Steps to solve
steps.description:
1. Right-click the home page (/) → Engagement tools → Discover content, then click "Session is not running" to start the scan.
2. Go to Target → Site map.
3. Select the lab URL → cgi-bin → phpinfo.php.
4. Right-click the request to phpinfo.php and copy its URL.
5. Open a new tab and paste it.
6. Press Ctrl+F and search for SECRET_KEY.
7. Copy the value of the SECRET_KEY variable and submit it as the solution.

title: Tmux Sessions: Keep Programs Running After You Close the Terminal
summary: Install tmux, detach from a running program, and come back to it later, even after closing your SSH session.

steps.title: Install tmux
steps.description: I used Ubuntu (Debian based) to install this.
steps.code:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install tmux -y

steps.title: Start a single tmux session
steps.description:
If you only need one session: start tmux and run your program. Detach with Ctrl + b, release both keys, then press d. You can now exit and log out.
After connecting to the system again, attach to the session you detached from.
steps.code:
tmux
python3 oneway.py
# Ctrl + b, release both keys, then d (detach)
exit
ssh root@ip          # connect to the system again
tmux attach          # attach to the most recently detached session

steps.title: Check tmux sessions and connect
steps.description:
List the existing sessions. Sessions without names are numbered 0, 1, 2 and so on.
Attach to the most recent session, or to a specific one (session 2 here).
steps.code:
tmux ls
tmux attach          # most recently detached session
tmux attach -t 2     # session 2

steps.title: Create and run multiple tmux sessions
steps.description:
Named sessions keep programs organized and easy to find. Create a session called MyFirstSession, run your program, detach, and attach again by name.
Create as many named sessions as you need.
steps.code:
tmux new -s MyFirstSession
python3 oneway.py
# Ctrl + b, release both keys, then d (detach)
tmux attach -t MyFirstSession

title: OverTheWire Bandit: Level 0 → 1
summary: Log in to the Bandit wargame over SSH for the first time and read the password for the next level from the readme file.

steps.title: SSH to bandit0
steps.description:
Username: bandit0
Password: bandit0
Host: bandit.labs.overthewire.org
Port: 2220

steps.title: Cat the readme file
steps.description: List the files in bandit0's home directory, then print the readme. It holds the password for bandit1.

steps.title: Bonus: copy remote files to Kali
steps.description:
You can copy the remote (Bandit) files to your own system (Kali). Open a new terminal in Kali and copy bandit0's readme file to your Desktop. When asked for a password, give bandit0's password.
Then go to the Desktop and cat the file.
